{"archetype": "cyclical_commodity", "runner_up": "secular_growth", "what_would_settle_it": "A period in the record in which industry DRAM/NAND average selling prices fell materially while Micron's revenue and gross margin still rose on data-center/HBM mix — that would show execution and mix, not the industry price cycle, driving the earnings swing and would move the classification to secular_growth; conversely, the FY2025 10-K showing the recast segments and a renewed ASP decline dragging consolidated gross margin back toward the 17% level would lock in cyclical_commodity.", "why": "FACT 1 [MU-10Q-Q3FY25 §Risk Factors — "Volatility in average selling prices"]: "In the past five years, annual percentage changes in DRAM average selling prices have ranged from plus low-teen percentage range to a minus high-40% range. In the past five years, annual percentage changes in NAND average selling prices have ranged from plus low-30% to a minus low-50% range."

FACT 2 [same section]: "In some prior periods, average selling prices for our products have been below our manufacturing costs and we may experience such circumstances in the future."

FACT 3 [§Consolidated Statements of Operations, Nine Months Ended]: "Net income (loss) | $5,338 | $(109)" — i.e. nine months ended May 29, 2025 versus nine months ended May 30, 2024.

FACT 4 [§MD&A Consolidated Gross Margin]: "improved to 38% for the first nine months of 2025 from 17% for the first nine months of 2024."

FACT 5 [§MD&A Consolidated Gross Margin]: "Our consolidated gross margin for the first nine months of 2024 reflected $987 million of benefit due to lower costs from the sale of inventories written down to their net realizable value in 2023."

FACT 6 [§Risk Factors — gross margins]: "in 2023, we recorded aggregate charges of $1.83 billion to write down the carrying value of our inventories to their estimated net realizable value."

FACT 7 [§Risk Factors — competition]: "We and our competitors generally seek to increase supply to address growing market demands, improve yields, and reduce die size, which could result in significant increases in worldwide supply and downward pressure on prices... Increases in worldwide supply of semiconductor memory and storage, if not accompanied by commensurate increases in demand, could lead to declines in average selling prices for our products."

FACT 8 [§Risk Factors — competition]: "We face intense competition in the semiconductor memory and storage markets from a number of companies, including Kioxia Holdings Corporation; Samsung Electronics Co., Ltd.; SK hynix Inc.; Sandisk Corporation; Yangtze Memory Technologies Co., Ltd. ("YMTC"); and ChangXin Memory Technologies, Inc. ("CXMT")."

FACT 9 [§Risk Factors — gross margins]: "A significant portion of our manufacturing costs are fixed and do not vary proportionally with changes in production output. As a result, lower utilization, lower wafer output, and corresponding increases in our per gigabit manufacturing costs could result in higher inventory carrying costs, and have had, and may continue to have, an adverse effect on our gross margins."

FACT 10 [§MD&A Results of Operations]: "Sales of DRAM products increased 60% primarily due to a high-40% range increase in average selling prices and a high-single-digit percent range increase in bit shipments" (first nine months of 2025 vs first nine months of 2024).

FACT 11 [§MD&A Results of Operations, Q3 2025 vs Q2 2025]: "Sales of NAND products increased 16% primarily due to a mid-20% range increase in bit shipments, partially offset by a high-single-digit percent range decrease in average selling prices."

FACT 12 [§Segment and Other Information, Operating income (loss), Nine Months Ended]: "SBU | 362 | (631)" and "MBU | 604 | (395)".

FACT 13 [§MD&A Liquidity]: "We estimate capital expenditures in 2025 for property, plant, and equipment, net of proceeds from government incentives, to be approximately $14 billion."

FACT 14 [§Consolidated Statements of Cash Flows, Nine Months Ended]: "Net cash provided by operating activities | 11,795 | 5,102" and "Expenditures for property, plant, and equipment | (10,199) | (5,266)".

FACT 15 [§Risk Factors — new technologies]: "If we or our competitors increase HBM supply at a rate that outpaces HBM demand, conversion of HBM capacity to supply other DRAM products could result in significant supply-demand imbalances. Due to the higher performance and more complex manufacturing process, HBM requires a higher number of wafers to produce the same number of bits as conventional DRAM in the same technology node. This could lead to declines in average selling prices for our DRAM products."

FACT 16 [§MD&A Industry Conditions]: "In 2024 and for the first nine months of 2025, we experienced substantial improvements in revenue, pricing, and margins as compared to 2023, reflecting demand growth, driven in part by deployment of AI, which resulted in a substantially improved industry supply and demand balance."

FACT 17 [§Certain Concentrations]: "Data center and networking | 55% | 30%" of total revenue for the nine months ended May 29, 2025 and May 30, 2024.

INFERENCE 18 (from 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 10): The reported swing from a nine-month net loss to $5,338 million of nine-month net income, and from a 17% to a 38% gross margin, is attributed by the company principally to average selling prices — DRAM ASPs up a "high-40% range" on high-single-digit bit growth — and the prior-year base itself contained a $987 million benefit from inventory written down in 2023. Earnings at this point in the record are therefore a poor guide to normal earnings.

INFERENCE 19 (from 7, 8, 9, 15): The company frames its own margin as governed by industry-wide supply additions against demand, with high fixed cost absorption, several scaled competitors and state-supported entrants, and it names its own differentiated product (HBM) as a potential source of the next supply-demand imbalance. That is the capacity-cycle mechanism, not a company-specific execution mechanism.

INFERENCE 20 (from 11, 12): Even inside this up-period, NAND ASPs fell sequentially and segment profitability reversed sign across periods (SBU $(631)M to $362M over nine months; $(9)M in Q3 2025 against $76M in Q3 2024), which is the within-window volatility the archetype predicts.

INFERENCE 21 (from 13, 14): Capital spending guided at roughly $14 billion for 2025 against $11,795 million of nine-month operating cash flow, with $10,199 million already spent on property, plant and equipment in nine months, is not "modest relative to cash generation." The compounder criterion fails on reinvestment intensity before any returns test is attempted.

FACT 22 [absence]: The bundle contains no computed_metrics block and no multi-year return-on-capital, ROIC, or cost-of-capital series.

INFERENCE 23 (from 22): The compounder criterion — "returns on capital have persisted above the cost of capital across the periods in the bundle" — cannot be tested here at all, so compounder is unavailable on its own stated terms, independent of Inference 21.

Why not the runner-up. INFERENCE 24 (from 16, 17, 10): The secular_growth case is real — data center and networking went from 30% to 55% of revenue and the company attributes demand growth in part to AI — but the criterion requires that growth dominates every other variable and that heavy reinvestment defers cash generation deliberately. FACT 14 shows operating cash flow of $11,795 million for nine months, i.e. cash generation is not deferred, and FACT 10 attributes the DRAM revenue increase primarily to price, not volume. The open question in the bundle is margin and price, which is the opposite of the secular_growth criterion.

Why not the others. FACT 25 [§Segment and Other Information]: revenue is disaggregated as "DRAM | $7,071 ... NAND | 2,155 ... Other (primarily NOR) | 75" with no rate base, no regulator setting returns, and no spread/reserve/capital-ratio disclosure; the balance sheet items presented are inventories, property, plant and equipment and debt. INFERENCE 26 (from 25): regulated_utility and financial are excluded. FACT 27 [§Contingencies]: "a jury rendered a verdict that Micron's memory modules infringe two asserted patents... and found that Micron should pay $425 million for infringement of the '912 patent and $20 million for infringement of the '417 patent" and "We are unable to predict the outcome of any of the matters noted above and cannot make a reasonable estimate of the potential loss or range of possible losses." INFERENCE 28 (from 27, 3): discrete legal events exist and are unquantified, but the company reports a continuing operating record with quarterly revenue of $9,301 million, so value does not rest on a small number of discrete events; binary_outcome is excluded.

Failure mode ranking. INFERENCE 29 (from 18, 19, 20): If the reader treats this as secular_growth and I am wrong, he capitalises a peak-cycle margin as a baseline and is exposed to the ASP range in FACT 1 and the below-cost-selling precedent in FACT 2. If he treats it as cyclical_commodity and I am wrong, he under-weights durable AI mix and misses upside. The first error is the more damaging, so the classification is cyclical_commodity.

ASSUMPTION A: That the four-business-unit segment figures quoted here remain comparable to what the FY2025 10-K will present. The filing states the opposite is intended — "The changes will require us to recast our segment reporting and we will report financial results under this new structure starting with our 2025 Annual Report on Form 10-K" — so any segment-level inference above (Inference 20) should be re-checked against the recast figures and rejected if they differ.

ASSUMPTION B: That "average selling prices" as used in the risk factor and in MD&A refer to the same industry-price variable. The bundle does not define them jointly; if they differ, Inference 18's attribution of the margin swing to the industry price cycle weakens.

DATA GAPS (not price-related): no multi-year annual income statement or full-year FY2023/FY2024 figures (only nine-month and quarterly columns); no bit-shipment or ASP levels in absolute terms, only directional ranges; no disclosure of industry-wide capacity or utilisation; no peer financials period-aligned or otherwise, so every comparison against Samsung, SK hynix, Kioxia, YMTC or CXMT in FACT 8 is unchecked rather than a result."}
